records.event: A U.S. F-15E was downed over Iran; both crew ejected.
Iranian reporting initially identified the aircraft as an F-35.
Tasnim reported the missing airman may have been captured, citing sources.
Tasnim headlined that a U.S. recovery effort had failed while its text said efforts had so far been futile.
Iranian fire hit two U.S. rescue helicopters during the search.
records.status: CONFIRMED CONTACT; NOT EQUIVALENT TO SHOOTDOWN

records.event: Provincial IRGC denied the second F-15E crewman was captured or detained.
Two MC-130s became disabled; U.S. personnel later destroyed disabled aircraft/equipment rather than leave sensitive systems behind.
Iran claimed its forces destroyed two C-130-family aircraft and two Black Hawks and brought the rescue to complete failure.
records.status: REAL LOSSES; FALSE ATTRIBUTION / OUTCOME CONTRADICTED

records.event: U.S. and independent reporting confirmed both F-15E crew members had been recovered in separate rescue efforts.
Press TV explicitly corrected the aircraft identity from F-35 to F-15E.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei speculated that the operation could have been a deception connected to stealing enriched uranium.
Press TV escalated the speculative possibility into a claim that the operation was not a rescue and targeted an Isfahan nuclear facility.
Press TV continued the alternative uranium-search / nuclear-operation explanation after the recovery outcome was public.
Fake visual “proof” circulated around the capture/shootdown narrative, including recycled 1991 footage and AI-generated images.
records.status: FALSE MEDIA; ORIGIN NOT ASSUMED OFFICIAL

method_rule: Chronology distinguishes provisional reporting from final mission outcome and separates Iranian kinetic contact from causal responsibility for U.S.-destroyed denial wreckage.
